Key long-term themes from recent reporting (mid-March to early April 2026):

- **Munitions depletion and replenishment timelines (years, not months):** The opening phase burned through thousands of high-value munitions (e.g., >5,000 in first 96 hours, including Tomahawks, Patriots, and JDAMs), consuming specific minerals like ~92 tons copper, 137 kg neodymium, 18 kg gallium, and tungsten per analysis. text:
In the 2026 market environment, gold miners face a "double squeeze" from rising input costs. While high gold prices provide a buffer, specific operational structures make certain companies far more vulnerable to sulfuric acid shortages and diesel price spikes.
1. Most Exposed to Sulfuric Acid Shortages
Sulfuric acid is primarily used in leaching operations (processing low-grade or oxide ores) and as a pH regulator in water treatment. Because 25% of global sulfur (the precursor to the acid) originates in the Middle East, the 2026 conflict has created a severe supply bottleneck.
Miners with Large Leaching Operations:
Barrick Gold (GOLD/ABX): Highly exposed due to its massive copper-gold leaching operations (e.g., Lumwana and projects in the DRC/Zambia). These regions import approximately 90% of their sulfur from the Middle East.
Newmont Corp (NEM): Vulnerable through its heap-leach operations in Nevada and South America. While some US operations have captive supply, global logistics disruptions are driving up the "delivered cost" of acid.
Ivanhoe Mines (IVN - TSX): Though primarily a copper/zinc producer, its gold-associated projects in Africa are in the "danger zone." Founder Robert Friedland recently noted that many African oxide operations have only 1–3 weeks of inventory before potential curtailments.
Geographic Risk:
Miners in Australia and Africa are most at risk as they lack the domestic "captive" acid production found in China or parts of the US.
2. Most Exposed to Diesel Price Spikes
Diesel typically accounts for 10% to 25% of a mine’s total operating costs. The exposure is determined by the Strip Ratio (how much waste rock must be moved to get to the gold) and the distance to the processing plant.
High Exposure: Large Open-Pit Miners
Open-pit mines rely on massive haul truck fleets (e.g., Cat 797s) that consume thousands of liters of diesel per shift.
Newmont (NEM): Operates some of the world's largest open-pit fleets. Recent reports indicate diesel price jumps of 70% have directly hit their bottom line, particularly at sites like Boddington (Australia) and Peñasquito (Mexico).
Kinross Gold (KGC): While it was the top performer recently, it is highly sensitive to energy. Its Tasiast (Mauritania) mine is a massive open-pit operation in a remote location where fuel logistics costs are extreme.
Barrick Gold (GOLD): Large-scale pits like Carlin (Nevada) and Pueblo Viejo (DR) are diesel-intensive. Management has noted that every $10/barrel increase in oil adds roughly $25/oz to their All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC).
Low Exposure: Underground & Grid-Connected Miners
Agnico Eagle (AEM): Many of its flagship Canadian mines (like LaRonde) are underground and connected to the Quebec hydroelectric grid. They use electric hoists and conveyors rather than diesel haul trucks for the majority of ore movement, shielding them from the "Hormuz diesel shock."
Evolution Mining (EVN): Similarly benefits from a higher proportion of underground operations and access to the Australian power grid for processing.

text:
New investor psychology and discipline:
This is really just a comment / observation.
Learner investor here from Australia. I recently moved my superannuation account ( I think it has some resemblance to a US 401K?) to one that I control because the industry offerings simply did not include any way for me to purchase physical metals (PMs) or to direct my investments into natural resource and commodities in ways that made sense to me.
I've only just got control of it and that was suddenly daunting.
I've made a list of my planned investments and their weightings within the portfolio . I've developed a phased program of investment (rather than committing all at once).
Yet I was suddenly faced with uncertainty. The silver, gold, oil and miners prices are presenting me with pause for thought.
Fear and greed are very noisily battling it out in my emotional reaction to this moment although it's one I've been planning for quite some time.
I'm going to slow down.
It looks to me like I'll have a safer time of it mental health / anxiety wise if I take very small bites at this volatile time in a small set of stocks that I feel most confident in at the levels they are trading at.
I'm watching silver and gold spot prices anticipating they'll react one way or another decisively if they get around their 200 DMA. I think that will give me more confidence to pursue my program with greater conviction.
My overall deliberate approach here is a long term - 5-10 year horizon but the cognitive load of making my first big investment forays and then seeing it immediately take a beating is one I'm mindful could be hard to take.
You've got to accept and then take risks - eyes wide open.. but perhaps I can also be a little careful with my own reaction to that process as well.
I'm sure this will get easier with practice.

text:
NGEx Minerals Ltd (OTC: NGXXF) posted phase 4 drill results on its Argentina Lunahuasi project. 


Lunahuasi is a monster copper-gold-silver project, with varying mineralization for each mineral throughout the deposit. It’s billed primarily as a copper story, but as this new drilling reveals, there’s a lot more going on.


At the main Lunahuasi drill site, three holes delivered significant copper results above 5% CuEq. 
These results are extraordinarily rich, as copper is economically mined at mineralization below 1%. 
But NGEx also hit another high grade zone just east of the main site. Total drilling revealed very rich deposits of: 
100.25m at 4.33% CuEq including 33.85m at 7.25% CuEq with high-grade sub-intervals up to 17.44% CuEq.
48.0m at 7.72% CuEq including 23.09m at 13.21% CuEq and a gold-rich strike of 7.3m at 15.90 g/t gold.
23.1m at 4.72% CuEq including 9.1m at 9.92% CuEq.
35.3m at 3.33% CuEq.
This phase 4 drilling is now complete, with over 27,000 meters drilled across 32 holes. Half of these holes still have assays pending, which means we’ll see another wave of potentially high grade results in the coming weeks. 
Next up is phase 5 drilling, which will begin in Q3 2026. 
Lunahuasi has the highest grade copper-gold drill results in years, and could very well prove to be one of the highest grade, and most profitable mines in the world.
